chunks: Build an LPF or HPF with one capacitor. The question: Build a LPF/HPF using a single capacitor.
One resistor and one capacitor can make either a low-pass or a high-pass filter. Only the connection changes.
For a low-pass, put the resistor in series with the signal and the capacitor from the output to ground. For a high-pass, swap them.
In both cases the corner frequency is 1 over (2 pi RC) .
Imagine a pond fed by a hose through a narrow pipe. The pond level follows slow changes in the inflow but smooths out quick ripples. That is a low-pass filter.
Now turn the idea around: pay attention only to how the level just changed, and ignore where it sits. That is the high-pass. Same two parts, different roles.
The analogy is loose, but the swap matches the circuit.
The same two parts in swapped positions. In the LPF the capacitor shunts high frequencies to ground; in the HPF the capacitor blocks low frequencies from reaching the resistor.
Low-pass filter: passes low frequencies and drops high ones. High-pass filter: passes high frequencies and drops low ones.
Corner frequency: the frequency where the output is down 3 decibels, f c equals 1 over (2 pi RC) . Shunt: connected from the signal line to ground.
Roll-off: the slope past the corner, 20 decibels per decade for one RC.
You want a 1 kilohertz low-pass. Pick C = 100 nanofarads. Then R equals 1 over (2 pi f C) equals 1 over (2 pi times 1000 times 10 to the -7) , about 1. 59 kilohms.
Wire R in series with the signal and C to ground. Swap the two parts and the same values give a 1 kilohertz high-pass. That is the whole idea.
